headline: Bank of England Raises Interest Rates for First Time in Three Years
summary: The Bank of England raised interest rates to 4% in its first hike in over three years to combat an inflation shock stoked by the Iran war, increasing tracker mortgage payments by an average of £30.72 a month.
why: The Bank of England sets monetary policy for the United Kingdom to maintain price stability, directly influencing borrowing costs, mortgage rates, and the valuation of the British pound.
